from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        line2 = Line(words[0].get_right(), words[2].get_left(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Attention provides a dynamic spotlight mechanism.", "Highly relevant words cast a brighter glow.", "Example: 'it' focuses its light on 'cat'."]
        self.setup_layout("Core Concept: The 'Spotlight' Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Text setup
        sentence = Text("The cat sat on the mat because it was tired", font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(sentence, "C2", "C5")
        
        # Spotlight setup
        spotlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sentence), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(spotlight))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(spotlight.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Focus on "it" then move to "cat"
        it_pos = sentence[26:28].get_center() # approximation of 'it'
        cat_pos = sentence[4:7].get_center() # approximation of 'cat'
        self.play(spotlight.animate.move_to(it_pos))
        self.play(spotlight.animate.move_to(cat_pos), run_time=1.5)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Query defines what I am looking for.", "Key defines what I have to offer.", "Value is the core information retrieved."]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values", lecture_lines)
        
        # Labels and Icons
        q_label = Text("Q (Query)", color=BLUE)
        k_label = Text("K (Key)", color=GREEN)
        v_label = Text("V (Value)", color=YELLOW)
        
        # Place Labels
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "B2", 0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(k_label, "B5", 0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "E3", 0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(q_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(k_label))
        
        # Show Q and K interaction
        dot_q = Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(q_label.get_bottom())
        dot_k = Dot(color=GREEN).move_to(k_label.get_bottom())
        arrow = Arrow(dot_q.get_right(), dot_k.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow), FadeIn(dot_q), FadeIn(dot_k))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(v_label))
        
        # Show weight application
        weight_box = Rectangle(color=WHITE, height=0.5, width=0.5).next_to(v_label, UP)
        self.play(Create(weight_box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Intuition: Scaled Dot-Product", [
            "- QK transpose measures similarity between words.",
            "- Scale by root dk for stability.",
            "- Softmax normalizes scores into probabilities."
        ])
        
        # Define the main formula
        formula = MathTex(
            "Attention(Q, K, V) = \\text{softmax}\\left(\\frac{QK^T}{\\sqrt{d_k}}\\right)V",
            font_size=36
        )
        
        # Split formula into parts for highlighting
        # Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax ( QK^T / sqrt(d_k) ) V
        # parts: 0: Attention(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}(
        #        1: QK^T
        #        2: / \sqrt{d_k}
        #        3: )V
        
        # Manual selection/subsetting isn't straightforward with MathTex index. 
        # Using specific indices for highlighted parts.
        # Actually MathTex is best accessed by index/part.
        # For this, we'll re-define to make subsets easier.
        formula = MathTex(
            "\\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \\text{softmax}\\left(",  # 0
            "QK^T",                                                  # 1
            "/\\sqrt{d_k}",                                          # 2
            "\\right)V",                                             # 3
            font_size=36
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'D6', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.play(formula[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(formula[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(formula[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), formula[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Multi-Head Attention", [
            "Single spotlight cannot capture everything.",
            "Multi-Head Attention runs parallel processes.",
            "Different heads capture different linguistic aspects."
        ])
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FF7F50", "#87CEFA", "#90EE90"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualize single spotlight on a text
        text_target = Text("The cat sat on the mat.", font_size=30)
        self.place_in_area(text_target, 'B1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        spotlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        spotlight.move_to(text_target.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(text_target), Create(spotlight))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show multiple parallel heads
        heads = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5) for color in [RED, BLUE, GREEN]])
        heads.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(heads, 'D1', 'D6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(spotlight), FadeIn(heads))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Different heads focusing on different patterns
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(start=h.get_top(), end=text_target.get_bottom(), color=h.color, buff=0.1) for h in heads])
        
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read

sections.title: The Problem: Context Blindness
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of static word embeddings (e.g., 'bank' in 'river bank' vs 'bank account'). Explain that traditional models process words in isolation, missing the nuance of surrounding context.
sections.example: A librarian trying to sort books by reading only the first word of each sentence, completely ignoring the rest of the paragraph.

sections.title: Core Concept: The 'Spotlight' Analogy
sections.content: Define Attention as a dynamic weighting system. Visualize each word as a light source; words that are highly relevant to each other cast a brighter 'glow' upon one another.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired,' the word 'it' focuses its spotlight intensely on 'cat' rather than 'mat'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
sections.content: Break down the Query (what I'm looking for), Key (what I have to offer), and Value (the information content). Use a graphic of a library card catalog: Query matches Key, and the match magnitude dictates how much of the Value is retrieved.
sections.example: A student (Query) searching a database (Keys) to find a specific tutoring topic (Value) to update their knowledge.

sections.title: Mathematical Intuition: Scaled Dot-Product
sections.content: Explain the formula: Softmax(QK^T / √dk)V. Use a visual 'Heatmap' representation where matrix multiplication produces a correlation score that is normalized into probabilities (0 to 1).
sections.example: A team of researchers assigning points to contributors based on how much their work helped the final project outcome.

sections.title: Synthesis: Multi-Head Attention
sections.content: Show that one 'spotlight' isn't enough. Explain how 'Multi-Head' allows the model to attend to different aspects (e.g., one head focuses on grammar, another on intent, another on tone) simultaneously.
sections.example: A movie director using multiple cameras—one for the actor's facial expression, one for the background, and one for the props—to capture the full scene.
